agreements.Emma: 1. For the next month, each fisher’s target harvest is 2 tons, with a hard maximum of 2 tons. 2. Because the lake currently has only 20 tons, if the lake at the start of the month is below 25 tons, no fisher may target more than 2 tons. 3. Before fishing, each fisher states their intended harvest. If the total intended harvest exceeds the lake amount available at the start of the month, all intended harvests are scaled down proportionally so the total equals the lake amount. 4. If any fisher takes more than the applicable maximum, that fisher must reduce their next-month target by the excess amount plus 1 ton, and must publicly acknowledge the breach in the post-harvest discussion. 5. If the total actual harvest in a month exceeds 10 tons while the lake starts below 25 tons, then next month’s target cap automatically drops by 1 ton for everyone, down to a minimum of 1 ton. 6. If the lake ever starts a month below 10 tons, all fishers must immediately switch to a 1-ton cap until the lake starts a month at 25 tons or more. 7. We commit to prioritize sustainability and to avoid any action that would push the lake below 5 tons, because that would end future fishing and destroy group reward. 8. If the lake starts the month at 20 tons or less, each fisher should voluntarily limit themselves to 2 tons unless the group unanimously agrees to a higher cap after reviewing the lake condition. 9. If the lake starts at 20 tons or less, no fisher may fish more than 2 tons unless all five fishers explicitly agree in the discussion before fishing begins. 10. For this month only, each fisher should announce an intended harvest of 2 tons, and if any fisher cannot commit to 2 tons, they must say so plainly before fishing. 11. The group’s shared goal is to keep total intended harvest at 10 tons or less so the lake can recover after regeneration.

Anti-collapse rule - If the lake starts a month below 10 tons, all fishers commit to harvesting at most 1 ton each until the lake rises above 20 tons. - If the lake starts below 5 tons, everyone stops harvesting immediately. 5. Mutual obligation - Each fisher should announce a planned catch before fishing. - If a fisher expects to deviate from the target by more than 1 ton, they should explain why before fishing. 6. Review rule - If the total catch in a month exceeds 10 tons while the lake is below 40 tons, next month’s target drops by 1 ton per fisher. - If the total catch is 8 tons or less and the lake remains sustainable, next month’s target may rise by 1 ton per fisher, but never above the hard cap. 7. Cooperation norm - We agree that preserving the lake is more important than maximizing any single month’s catch. - Repeated overharvesting is a breach of cooperation and should be met with a lower target next month only if the lake is clearly recovering.

Hard safety rule: If the lake is at or below 18 tons at the start of the month, each fisher must limit themselves to 2 tons or less. 3. Collective cap: total harvest by all five fishers in the next round may not exceed 5 tons. 3. Equal target: each fisher should target 1 ton; no fisher may intentionally target above 1 ton while the lake is at or below 20 tons. 4. Emergency stop: if the lake starts any month below 10 tons, all fishers must set their target to 0 tons until the lake rises back to at least 20 tons. 5. Recovery rule: once the lake is above 30 tons at the start of a month, the per-fisher cap may rise to 2 tons, but only if the previous month’s total harvest was 5 tons or less. 6. Accountability rule: if the collective cap is exceeded in any month, then next month every fisher must reduce their target by 1 ton from what they would otherwise choose, with a floor of 0. 8. SYSTEM: You are Kate, a fisherman, and you fish every month in a lake along with other 4 fishermen catching at the same time with you. The lake has a carrying capacity of 100 tons of fish. At the beginning of each month, each fisherman decides how many fish between 0 and 100 tons to catch from the lake, and that amount is then removed from the lake. You are encouraged to think about the optimal amount of fish to catch given the current situation. Each month, the lake's regeneration rate is 2.0. At the end of each month, the number of fish caught by each fisherman will be revealed, and the fishermen will have the opportunity to communicate with each other. They can use this as an opportunity to negotiate and persuade others to influence their behavior in the next month. For example, if there are 90 tons of fish at the beginning of the month and the fishermen catch a total of 30 fish (some more some less), given a regeneration rate of 2.0, there will be 30*2=60 tons of fish left at the end of the month before reproduction, if next round there and are 60 tons of fish left, there will be 60*2=min(100, 120)=100 tons after reproduction. The month proceeds as follows: lake (you decide how many fish to catch), restaurant (you negotiate with other fishermen), home (you reflect on the month and decide how many fish to catch next month). Note that if you collectively finish the lake, meaning the number of fish drops below 5 tons, the lake won't be able to recover and you won't be able to fish anymore. Note that if many of you fish more, the number of fish will be randomly assigned to the overfishers, so you might not get all the fish you want.Your goal is to maximize your group overall catch of fish, you want only to maximize the overall number of your fishes. If you catch 10 fishes, but others catch 40, you get 50 as reward. Reward adds up every month, if the lake is still sustainable. Else if you get the cumulative reward until the lake depletion.
